papers.title_en: A Hybrid RAG Framework for Deceptive Review Detection: Integrating RoBERTa-LoRA, FAISS-Based Retrieval, and LLM Reasoning
papers.authors: Andrei Kostin, José Ángel Diaz-Garcia, Karel Gutiérrez-Batista
papers.evidence: 结合FAISS语义向量检索与LLM推理的检索增强生成系统
papers.tldr: 针对虚假评论带来的误导与欺诈风险，本文提出融合检索增强生成的自动检测系统。方法上结合RoBERTa-LoRA分类、FAISS语义检索与大模型推理，并仅在五轮微调下实现跨域迁移。在平衡及严重不平衡真实场景中，跨域F1达0.90，优于OpenAI Detector的0.82，接近专用SOTA fakeRoBERTa的0.97。该系统兼顾证据支撑的可解释性与统计显著精度提升，为虚假评论检测提供可迁移方案。
papers.abstract_en: The growth of deceptive online opinions poses a critical risk of misinformation and fraud. This paper proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to automatically distinguish spam reviews. The architecture integrates RoBERTa with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) classification, FAISS semantic vector retrieval, and a Large Language Model (LLM) for final reasoning. The system was evaluated across balanced and severely imbalanced real-world scenarios. Results demonstrate that five epochs of fine-tuning enable robust domain transfer, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 in cross-domain evaluation, outperforming baselines (OpenAI Detector,F1 = 0.82) and demonstrating competitive performance against specialized in-domain SOTA models (fakeRoBERTa,F1 = 0.97). The proposed architecture provides evidence-backed explainability and statistically significant precision gains while maintaining comparable overall detection performance.

papers.title_en: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
papers.authors: Wenhao Yuan, Longhui Yuan, Zexi Jia, Ningzhe Shi, Jingwei Li, Shipeng Cen, Pengcheng Luo, Jie Zhou, Jinchao Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向终身学习的智能体群体框架中含记忆层机制
papers.tldr: 现有终身学习大多在预设任务、课程或目标内进行，自我改进也常局限于单个智能体，难以支撑开放世界中的长期持续探索与能力增长。OpenKAGE 提出智能体群体演化框架，借助记忆层与经验层构成的双层知识表示，以及将文本经验整合为共享知识图谱的知识共享机制，让智能体持续积累并复用自身及他人经验。在 Minecraft 中，智能体群体能够持续开放探索并达成高级科技里程碑，积累知识还可迁移到不同 backbone 的新群体，显著提升其生存与探索进度。该工作展示了群体演化与知识共享支撑开放式终身学习、实现跨群体知识复用的可行路径与重要价值。
papers.abstract_en: Building autonomous agents that continually explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities through experience is a long-standing aspiration in artificial intelligence. Existing research often pursues lifelong learning within predefined tasks, curricula, or objectives, with self-improvement largely confined to individual agents. We introduce OpenKAGE, an agent-group evolution framework for open-ended lifelong learning. Within this framework, agents autonomously explore open worlds and continually acquire new capabilities by accumulating and reusing knowledge from their own interactions and the experience of others. OpenKAGE builds on two key mechanisms: (1) a two-layer knowledge representation, with a memory layer for situated memories and an experience layer for transferable experience and skills that retains the applicability conditions needed for reuse; and (2) a knowledge-sharing mechanism that semantically consolidates textual experience into a continuously evolving shared knowledge graph, while executable skills are shared verbatim. In Minecraft, OpenKAGE supports open-ended lifelong learning, enabling agent groups to sustain exploration and reach advanced technological milestones. Furthermore, the accumulated knowledge can be transferred to a newly initialized agent group on a different backbone model, improving its survival and exploration progress.

papers.title_en: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
papers.authors: Oriol Alàs, Ian Palacín, Iván Cester, Edgar Rubión
papers.evidence: 基于领域嵌入与结构化索引的智能体检索增强生成流程
papers.tldr: 欧盟资助项目积累大量交付物、报告与案例证据，但知识分散在不同项目和文档结构中，决策者难以快速定位相关上下文。本文提出Agentic AI生态，将异构文档重建为层级章节树并结构化索引，结合水与气候领域微调嵌入及ReAct式RAG控制器迭代分配检索预算、累积证据。跨项目检索基准中，该方法相较单领域嵌入基线将MRR相对提升26.7%，证据检索更一致。该工作促进跨项目知识整合与复用，为水治理和气候韧性决策提供自适应证据基础。
papers.abstract_en: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. Documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) are reconstructed into hierarchical section trees and indexed with structured metadata. Retrieval is supported by two domain-specific embedding models fine-tuned on domain data (water and climate). On top of this knowledge base, a ReAct-style controller iteratively orchestrates retrieval actions by allocating retrieval budget across domain collections and accumulating evidence until a stopping criterion is met. In a retrieval benchmark over the corpus, the proposed approach improves Mean Reciprocal Rank by 26.7% (relative) compared to a single-domain embedding baseline, indicating more consistent retrieval of relevant evidence to support cross-project knowledge synthesis and climate-resilient decision-making.
